paite: Itali gam a long a pai ding thu ahihpuktak un, Paul leh henta dang kuate hiam Augusta pawl a sepaih zaheutu, amin Julias akemsak uhi.
heading: Rome Zuan A Paul Zinna
english: When it was determined that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.

paite: Huan Adramittium kho long, Asia gam tuipi piau a kho omte tawn ding ah ka tuang ua, tuipi ah ka paita uhi. Ka kiang uah Masidonia gam a mi Aristarkhas, Thessalonika khomi a-om hi.
english: Embarking in a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail to places on the coast of Asia, we put to sea, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica being with us.

paite: Azing in Sidon khua ka tawn uhi. Julias in Paul alimbawl ngial a, kihihhalh ding in alawmte kiang ah apawtsak hi.
english: The next day, we touched at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly and gave him permission to go to his friends and refresh himself.

paite: Huai a kipan in tuipi ah ka pai nawn ua, huih in ahi lou lam a hon mut ziak in Kupra tuikulh zul huih hatlouhna lam ah ka tai uhi.
english: Putting to sea from there, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

paite: Silisia gam leh Pamphilia gamzul tuipi ka khen nung un, Lisia gam a Mira khua ka tung uhi.
english: When we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.

paite: Huai ah sepaih zaheutupa'n Aleksandria kho long Itali gam tawn ding amu a; huai ah hon tuangsak hi.
english: There the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy, and he put us on board.

paite: Ni tampi, awlawl in ka pai ua, Knidas kho zawn haksapi in ka tung teitei ua, huih in hon sawnkik ziak in Salmoni zuan in Krit tuikulh zul huih hatlouhna lam ah ka tai uhi.
english: When we had sailed slowly many days, and had come with difficulty opposite Cnidus, the wind not allowing us further, we sailed under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.

paite: Haksatak in tui geigei ah ka pai ua, Longkhawlna Kilawm achih mun uh ka tungta ua; huai kiang ah Lasea khua a-om hi.
english: With difficulty sailing along it we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.

paite: Huan ni tampi abei tak ziak in leh long a pai alauhuai ziak in, An Ngawl ni akhengta ngal a, Paul in amau athuhilh a, akiang uah,
heading: Paul In Long Siat Ding Agenkhol
english: When much time had passed and the voyage was now dangerous because the Fast had now already gone by, Paul admonished them

paite: "Pute aw, tua long a tuangte siatna leh manthatna thupitak i tung ua tung ding ahi chih ka thei a, avante leh long tung ah kia ka chi kei a, eimah tung ah leng ka chi ahi," achi hi.
english: and said to them, “Sirs, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives.”

paite: Himahleh sepaih zaheutu in Paul thugen sang in longpu leh long neipa thu agingta zaw hi.
english: But the centurion gave more heed to the master and to the owner of the ship than to those things which were spoken by Paul.

paite: Phalbi douna ding in longkhawlna aginat louh ziak in atamzaw in huai a kipan a tuipi a paikhiak a, bangchi hiam bek a Phoenik khua tun teitei a, huai lai a phalbi dou asawmpih ua; Phoenik ahihleh Krit tuikulh a longkhawlna khat ahi a, simtum leh maltum lam doh ahi.
english: Because the haven was not suitable to winter in, the majority advised going to sea from there, if by any means they could reach Phoenix and winter there, which is a port of Crete, looking southwest and northwest.

paite: Sim huih awlawl a ahong nuntak in adeihlam uh mu akisa ua, sikkip akhaikhia ua, Krit tuikulh zulzul ah apai uhi.
heading: Tui Tung Ah Huihpi
english: When the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close to shore.

paite: Himahleh sawt lou nung in huih hattak, Euroklidon kichi, gam lam a kipan in ahong nung hi.
english: But before long, a stormy wind beat down from shore, which is called Euroclydon.

paite: Long ahon mutkhata a, huihlam angat theih louhtak in ka khahta ua, hon mutleng hon mutlengta hi.
english: When the ship was caught and couldn’t face the wind, we gave way to it and were driven along.

paite: Kauda tuikulh neuchik petmah pansan in huih hatlouhna lam ah ka tai ua, haksatak in long neu ka bitsak thei ham uhi.
english: Running under the lee of a small island called Clauda, we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat.

paite: Akaihkhiak nung un panpihna khaute khawng azang ua, long nuailam ah vial kawm in akhih uhi. Puanzakna bangkim apuksak ua, huchi lou in zaw Sirtis piaunel kip lou a lenlut alau ua, huchi in huih mutdan dungzui in apai uhi.
english: After they had hoisted it up, they used cables to help reinforce the ship. Fearing that they would run aground on the Syrtis sand bars, they lowered the sea anchor, and so were driven along.

paite: Tuikihot in hon sep ek ziak in, azing in tui lak ah long a vante apaikheta uhi.
english: As we labored exceedingly with the storm, the next day they began to throw things overboard.

paite: Huan ani thum ni in, amau khut in long vante apaikhe nawnta uhi.
english: On the third day, they threw out the ship’s tackle with their own hands.

paite: Huan ni tampi nisa leh aksi leng akimu kei a, huihpi hat petmah in hon nuai a, hin himhim ka lamen nawn kei uhi.
english: When neither sun nor stars shone on us for many days, and no small storm pressed on us, all hope that we would be saved was now taken away.

paite: Huan an ne lou a sawttak a-om nung un, alak uah Paul adingh a, "Pute aw, Krit tuikulh a kiphel lou dia, ka thu ngaikhia hi le uchin hiai siatna leh manthatna tuah louh ding hi zen a.
english: When they had been long without food, Paul stood up in the middle of them and said, “Sirs, you should have listened to me, and not have set sail from Crete and have gotten this injury and loss.

paite: Himahleh tu'n ah leng khamuangtak a om ding in ka hon hanthawn lai hi. Na lak uah kuamah in hinna na mangsak kei ding uh, long zaw amangthang ding.
english: Now I exhort you to cheer up, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.

paite: Amah Pathian a ka hih a, a-nna leng ka sep, amah angel tuzan in ka kiang ah ahong dingh a, ka kiang ah,
english: For there stood by me this night an angel, belonging to the God whose I am and whom I serve,

paite: 'Paul, lau ke'n, Kaisar ma ah na dingh ding. Ngai in, long a na kiang a zin tengteng leng Pathian in ahon pia hi,' ahon chi hi.
english: saying, ‘Don’t be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar. Behold, God has granted you all those who sail with you.’

paite: Huaiziak in Pute aw, khamuangtak in om un, Pathian ka gingta hi, hon hilh bang in a-om ding hi.
english: Therefore, sirs, cheer up! For I believe God, that it will be just as it has been spoken to me.

paite: Himahleh bang tuikulh hiam ah zaw ahon lenkhe ding," achi hi.
english: But we must run aground on a certain island.”

paite: Zan sawm-le-li achin zan in Adria tuipi ah huih in alanglang ah ahon mutleng leng lai hi. Zankim lai in, long mite'n koi gam hiam tung dek in akithei uhi.
heading: Long Siatna
english: But when the fourteenth night had come, as we were driven back and forth in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors surmised that they were drawing near to some land.

paite: Huchi in tui thukdan ateh ua, laam sawmnih hi in athei ua, huan sawt louchik in ateh nawn ua, laam sawm-le-nga hi in athei uhi.
english: They took soundings and found twenty fathoms. After a little while, they took soundings again, and found fifteen fathoms.

paite: Huan longmei lam ah sikkip li akhia ua, huchi lou in zaw suang se mun ah hon lenkhe zenzen kha ding chih alau ua; huan khovak kal angaklahtak in a-om uhi.
english: Fearing that we would run aground on rocky ground, they let go four anchors from the stern, and wished for daylight.

paite: Huan long mite'n long malam a sikkipte khiak ding bawl a kineih in tuipi ah long neu akhia ua, long taisan atum uhi.
english: As the sailors were trying to flee out of the ship and had lowered the boat into the sea, pretending that they would lay out anchors from the bow,

paite: Hiai lai in Paul in, sepaih zaheutu leh sepaihte kiang ah, "Hiaite long a a-om gige kei uleh abit kei ding uh," achi hi.
english: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, “Unless these stay in the ship, you can’t be saved.”

paite: Huchi in sepaihte'n long neu khaute a-attat ua, akhahta uhi.
english: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat and let it fall off.

paite: Khovak kuan in, Paul in an ne ding in mi tengteng asawl a, "Tuni bangmah ne lou a na om ua, an na ngawlna uh ani sawm-le-li ni ahita.
english: While the day was coming on, Paul begged them all to take some food, saying, “Today is the fourteenth day that you wait and continue fasting, having taken nothing.

paite: Huaiziak in an ne ding in ka hon sawl chiat ahi; na damna ding uh; na lak uah kuamah asamzang khat leng amangthang kei ding,” achi hi.
english: Therefore I beg you to take some food, for this is for your safety; for not a hair will perish from any of your heads.”

paite: Huai thu agen khit in tanghou ala a, Pathian kiang ah kipahthu agen khit in, mi tengteng ma ah abalkham a, ane panta hi.
english: When he had said this and had taken bread, he gave thanks to God in the presence of all; then he broke it and began to eat.

paite: Amau leng khamuangtak in a-om ua, an ane samta uhi.
english: Then they all cheered up, and they also took food.

paite: Long a mite ka vek un zanih sawmsagih-le-guk ka hi uhi.
english: In all, we were two hundred seventy-six souls on the ship.

paite: An anek kham khit un, tuipi ah buh apai ua, long ahihzang deuh uhi.
english: When they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, throwing out the wheat into the sea.

paite: Huan ni asuah in, koi lai gam ahia chih athei kei ua; himahleh, koi lai longkhawlna hiam piautak nei khat amu ua, huai tung ah ahihtheih uleh long taikhiaksak atum uhi.
english: When it was day, they didn’t recognize the land, but they noticed a certain bay with a beach, and they decided to try to drive the ship onto it.

paite: Huan sikkip khihnate a-attat ua, tuipi ah anusia ua; huchih lai mah in kaihheina khihnate aphel ua, huih mut ding in malam puanzak akaitou ua; piautak azuanta uhi.
english: Casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time untying the rudder ropes. Hoisting up the foresail to the wind, they made for the beach.

paite: Himahleh tuikihot khauh nih kituahna mun ah ka lutkha zenzen ua, long in lei hetkha in, huan, long mailam atang bikbekta a, hihtat zoh louh in a-omta a, tuikihot ahat ziak in longmei lam akekgawpta hi.
english: But coming to a place where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground. The bow struck and remained immovable, but the stern began to break up by the violence of the waves.

paite: Huan hentate, tui liau galkai khattou a om kha ding ua, ataimang kha ding uh chih alauh man un sepaihte'n amaute hihlup mai asawm uhi.
english: The soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, so that none of them would swim out and escape.

paite: Himahleh sepaih zaheutu in Paul humhing a-ut a, athiltup uh akham a; tuileuh siam peuhmah tuipi a tawmkhiak a gam na kai masa ding leh,
english: But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, stopped them from their purpose, and commanded that those who could swim should throw themselves overboard first to go toward the land;

paite: midang akhen singpek tung leh akhen long van tung a kitholh galkai ding in thu apia hi. Huchi in avek un gam ah bittak in agalkai vek uhi.
english: and the rest should follow, some on planks and some on other things from the ship. So they all escaped safely to the land.
